subject: warnings about values for cyclic RW1/RW2 models

messages.author: 958272119e13f0e7
messages.subject: warnings about values for cyclic RW1/RW2 models
parts:
Dear R-INLA,

I am fitting a model to a set of weekly data (where I don't have values in every week) with the following formula

f.climatology <- n.catch ~ f(week,model="rw2",cyclic=TRUE,values=1:52)

I want to have a smoother based on week number that loops around from the last week of the year to the first, and that handles the unobserved weeks properly (by estimating a value there based on neighbouring values).

However, I get the following warning message when fitting the model:

*** Warning ***    Model[rw2] in Section[seasonal.bin] has cyclic = TRUE but values != NULL.
*** Warning ***    Cylic = TRUE is not implemented for non-equal spaced values.
*** Warning ***    Assume values are equal spaced.

The documentation for both the RW1 and RW2 models describe the value argument as follows:

The (optional) argument
values
is a numeric or factor vector giving the values assumed by the
covariate for which we want the effect to be estimated. See next example for an application.


Unfortunately there isn't an example in the documentation. Does the way that I have set the model up look correct? Why then does the warning appear?

Best wishes,

Mark

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] warnings about values for cyclic RW1/RW2 models
parts:
Thanks for your email and for raising this issue.

In short, if you know what you do then you can ignore this warning. for
general locations, then cyclic=T is not well/uniquly defined and it
then use the definition from the equal spaced locations.

I did the required coding, and checked it the locations equal spaced,
and if so, then its fine and no need for the warning.

It will be available in the next build.

thx
H



$ hg commit -m "Added a proper check for the cyclic=TRUE warning, so it
now only give the warning if the locations are not equally spaced.
Thanks to MRP."
